recent_candidates.title: Schumer’s 2028 decision
recent_candidates.excerpt: Presented by OpenAI: The unofficial guide to official Washington. Nov 22, 2026 View in browser By Jonathan Martin Presented by With help from Eli Okun, Ali Bianco and Irie Sentner DRIVING THE DAY Sen. Chuck Schumer may not need to state the obvious — that he plans to retire in 2028 — to claim the votes needed to lead his caucus again. But he should anyway. Schumer finds himself in an awkward position ahead of his leadership election next month. He doesn't want to immediately make himself a lame duck, but he'd smooth his path back to being majority leader one more time if he assured his colleagues they were only signing a two-year lease. The soon-to-be 76-year-old had gone to the then-81-year-old Joe Biden in the summer of 2024 to say it was time to go. He can now choose the course he and so many in his party now wish Biden had taken before the former president's disastrous attempt to cling to power. By being candid about his intentions, Schumer can tamp down his party's factional fights, which began in the form of Sen. Chris Van Hollen's challenge two weeks after the midterms. Even if he easily dispatches Van Hollen next month, questions about Schumer's future will linger over Democrats in New York, Washington and beyond through 2027. It's not as though President Donald Trump's final two years, with Stephen Miller running the West Wing, augur a season of fruitful lawmaking. Join to Listen Online < Read Online < Michael Reneau•Daniel K. Williams / November 22, 2026 You’re reading Dispatch Faith, our weekly newsletter exploring the intersection of religion and public life from leading writers of various faiths. Hi and happy Sunday. I spent some time this week at an Interfaith America conference in Philadelphia celebrating the 250th anniversary of the birth of the country, hearing about what leaders in a variety of sectors are doing to safeguard the country’s heritage of religious freedom and pluralism—the commitment to the idea that people who believe radically different things can actually be citizens of the same country. One theme that stuck out to me: Living together requires us to lean into these natural tensions rather than shirking them. Only by leaning in can we have the big discussions—or arguments—and move forward. In today’s Dispatch Faith, historian Daniel K. Williams hits on a big tension in the wake of this month’s midterms: that the prospect of a new religious left is good for our politics and even good for the conservative Christians (like me) who have big differences on policy and, yes, theology, with Christians on the political left. recent_candidates.title: Old questions
recent_candidates.excerpt: friends, I read your Tankas in queues, at home, waiting for news of home, alone. I’m moved by what form holds — whole worlds in symbols, syllables Now, on to other matters. I come to you with a Tiny Question: What is the soul? Or, to be more personable: What is the soul for you? This is the question that dogged medieval mystics and murders and exiles and excommunications. One group thought one thing; another group thought another. If the soul is the Mind+Will+Emotions, which is first in that order? Lives were lost in the scandals. It wasn’t all esoteric nonsense, of course: at the heart of it was the question whether illumination could be reached through reason, or whether it always came from outwith. The scandals that battered medieval Europe were wide-reaching in their intellectual sources: Christian theologians read and grappled with the frameworks provided by Muslim and Jewish theologians. They all were wrestling with the texts and mindsets given by mathematicians and philosophers of centuries before too. Toledo was a place of negotiation between scholars from these traditions: each in respect of the argumentation of the other. Our Poetry Unbound in Conversation episode this week looks at some of these questions. recent_candidates.author: Max Tani

But during a Q&A Saturday night at the Darryl F. Zanuck Theater on the Fox studio lot, Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder said that the THR story’s framing and wording was inaccurate, and that none of the documentary’s subjects were paid, according to one person in attendance. An A24 spokesperson declined to comment. But a studio source said that after Evans negotiated a profit participation deal, he ultimately relinquished his right to it. He and A24 mutually agreed to donate the proceeds to charity; as a part of the deal, the source said, Evans gave up his right to participate in the film’s profits. recent_candidates.title: High-profile events businesses can strain media companies’ trust and credibility
recent_candidates.author: Max Tani
recent_candidates.excerpt: The News Semafor is facing scrutiny for hiring high-profile Washington consultants to assist with event bookings, a revelation that underscores the murkiness embedded into a high-level convening business that’s become a vital and growing revenue source for some global media companies. As online web traffic and the associated advertising dollars have diminished across the industry, publishers have leaned into sponsored in-person events to support their newsrooms. The growing importance of these events has raised thorny standards and ethics questions regarding sponsors who pay to be onstage at places like Fortune, The Wall Street Journal and The Atlantic — even if their sessions are clearly labeled as sponsored — or regarding media CEOs who strike deals with advertisers while interviewing those same CEOs. Of the last decade’s crop of digital media outlets, none have leaned further into the events-driven business than Semafor, which has hosted hundreds of high-profile gatherings since launching in late 2022. While Semafor primarily relies on an in-house events team to secure bookings of business, political and government leaders, for its flagship April gathering, Semafor World Economy, the Washington Post reported on Thursday that the company enlisted a handful of external consultants to recruit politicians for onstage interviews. Among the consultants were former Trump advisers Jason Miller and Kellyanne Conway, as well as former Kamala Harris and Joe Biden adviser Adrienne Elr

recent_candidates.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ marks a turning point for the series
recent_candidates.author: Manny Fidel
recent_candidates.excerpt: The highest-grossing film of all time, , grossed $2.9 billion during its theatrical run. , the long-awaited next installment of the video game franchise, recorded $3.8 billion in sales on its first day. In a rave review, The New York Times called it “a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful,” while The Washington Post gushed that the game was “an astonishing American epic.” The Miami Heat released special-edition Vice City jerseys. The record-setting release represents the cultural acceptance of a franchise that was once the center of a backlash to violent video games. During a press conference in 2005, then-Sen. Hillary Clinton said that the “disturbing material in and other games like it is stealing the innocence of our children,” and The House of Representatives passed a resolution (by a bipartisan 355-21 vote) asking the FTC to investigate Rockstar, the studio that makes. The late Sen. Joe Lieberman (who some GTA fans suspect is parodied by the weedy in-universe character “Chaz Lieberman”) denounced GTA for years. The franchise outlasted and outgrew the backlash. The game added layers of narrative tenderness in between some of the brutal and comic setpieces, and expanded its range of playable tasks into the comically mundane, like painting your character’s house and picking up groceries for his girlfriend. recent_candidates.title: Bessent warns on Fed hike as AI bubble fears mount
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Sunday that the Federal Reserve risks hurting the economy by overtightening policy , days after a tech-induced market correction intensified concerns that the AI bubble could be bursting. Traders have pared back expectations of a half-point hike on Dec. 9, after Anthropic’s record-setting IPO and a strong run of tech earnings failed to boost sentiment; some investors fear the Fed could be “ tightening into an economic slowdown when both earnings and AI investment have peaked,” an analyst told Reuters. “Don’t believe anyone who says the AI boom is different,” a Bloomberg columnist argued, noting the busts that followed railroads, electrification, and the internet. “ Be prepared for the tide to go out .” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Claude helps topple Riemann problem
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: Two independent groups said they verified an Anthropic mathematician’s Claude-assisted proof of the nearly 170-year-old Riemann Hypothesis , as AI appeared to bulldoze yet another long-unsolved problem. “If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics ,” a Fields Medal winner told Nature of the Riemann breakthrough, which involves how evenly prime numbers appear en route to infinity: “I think it’s likely to be correct.” Coming on the heels of OpenAI releasing more than 300 mathematical proofs developed with human oversight, the Riemann proof is a “remarkable thing we might see a lot more of in the future,” a math professor told The New York Times, “where there is a very skillful jockey riding a really fast horse .” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: US spy chief calls Nvidia chips 'jewels'
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: US intelligence chief Jay Clayton said Sunday that Washington was probing the alleged Chinese spy linked to ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as scrutiny of Beijing’s efforts to secure American chips intensified. Nvidia chips are the “ jewel… that everybody wants ,” Clayton told ABC’s , as The New York Times reported that China’s spy agency has helped mainland companies acquire advanced chips to drive domestic chip innovation . While Chinese AI labs would prefer to keep using Nvidia chips in the short run, Brookings expert Kyle Chan told Bloomberg’s podcast that US export controls have fueled Beijing’s efforts “to replicate the entire global semiconductor supply chain in China, which I don’t think any country has ever done before.” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: COP31 collapse highlights Africa's climate finance woes
recent_candidates.author: Jeronimo Gonzalez
recent_candidates.excerpt: The deep divisions between nations over climate finance, which contributed to the breakdown of COP31 talks, underscored the funding challenges facing African countries as they try to adapt to a warming planet. Although the continent contributes only 4% of global emissions , nine of the 10 most climate-vulnerable countries are in Africa , according to one study. In 2022, the continent received far less than the $190 billion required annually in climate funding, and its biggest economy alone needs more than $15 billion to fully implement climate adaptation policies over the next decade. While South Africa is experiencing heat waves that are damaging agricultural output, its grid remains heavily reliant on the sorts of fossil fuels that contribute the most to global emissions. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

recent_candidates.title: US, China eye ‘joint guardrails’ on AI
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: President Donald Trump said Friday that the US would work with China to develop “ joint guardrails ” on AI, after an anti-tech backlash helped drive a historic rebuke of Republicans in midterm elections. After Trump earlier warned that regulation could “ stifle ” innovation, his latest remarks reflect the accommodations that even the most bullish AI proponents are making, with protests against data center construction spreading to Europe, Japan, and India . Meanwhile, harsher US export controls are expected to slow China’s AI development, as OpenAI tightened Chinese access to its models. As barriers to technology sharing build, it’s “increasingly looking like… the real-life impacts of AI take longer to materialize than we initially expected,” Semafor’s San Francisco bureau chief wrote. — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: COP’s fossil fuel consensus falls apart
recent_candidates.author: Tim McDonnell
recent_candidates.excerpt: The News The COP31 climate summit in Türkiye collapsed on Sunday without agreement on a final deal, over deep disagreement over the negotiations’ most basic provision — the first time the talks ended unsuccessfully since calamitous 2009 meetings. After negotiations stretched to their longest in three decades, Murat Kurum, the summit president, finally acknowledged that a meeting meant to drive forward the “implementation” of countries’ existing carbon-cutting commitments could not even agree on what their overarching goal should be. “There is no consensus on this document,” he said, marking the first time for COP to conclude without an agreement since the calamitous 2009 summit in Copenhagen. “Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted.” Tim’s view The breakdown effectively marks the demise of a 2023 consensus, reached in Dubai, on the long-term phaseout of fossil fuels in the global economy. The years since then have been marked by successive global energy crises, including the biggest oil and gas supply disruption in history. While these crises have driven a faster pivot from fossil fuels in some importing countries, they have reinforced others’ conviction that more, not less, investment is required in the legacy energy system for the sake of security and affordability. COP31 shows that climate action was a casualty of that turmoil. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said it was targeting U.S. bases and air defense radars, but the government of Bahrain said the strikes caused a fire to a civilian industrial facility. Tehran said the attack was retaliation for U.S. violations of Iranian airspace and strikes on a radar installation. The commander-in-chief of the IRGC, Major General Ahmad Vahidi, said any violations of Iran’s airspace will be met by a “firm and decisive response,” Iranian media reported Sunday. Vahidi visited an underground base on Saturday to unveil a new dual-missile launcher, warning the U.S. against restarting major hostilities. President Donald Trump on Saturday morning told Fox News he wants to strike a lasting agreement with Iran over its nuclear program. “I’m going to make a deal that is going to be permanent,” Trump said . “I’m not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon.” The statement marks an apparent reversal from about a week and half ago, when Trump said, “we don’t need a deal with Iran.” Washington and Tehran continue to exchange diplomatic messages and Qatar has stepped up its mediation efforts in recent days. recent_candidates.author: Theodore Dalrymple
recent_candidates.excerpt: Culture Keynesianism for the Gender-Dysphoric Why should the rest of the population pay for the individual’s mere whims? On the other side is a clinic run by the tattooist’s brother, in which you can, at considerable expense, have your tattoos removed. This is an excellent economic model that no doubt adds to the country’s gross domestic product—a model which, on the other hand, establishes pretty conclusively that the GDP is a severely limited measure of a country’s well-being. recent_candidates.title: South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran
recent_candidates.author: Mera Aladam
recent_candidates.excerpt: South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said that a motion to extend the deployment of the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit in the Gulf of Aden did not amount to involvement in the US-Israeli war on Iran. The minister told lawmakers that the deployment was not indirect military participation in the conflict, but instead cited a rise in piracy alongside efforts to protect South Korean ships and citizens using the maritime route.

recent_candidates.title: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
recent_candidates.author: Mera Aladam
recent_candidates.excerpt: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria? Turkey's foreign minister has warned that Israel could launch a military operation in Syria, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention. Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials. "There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said. The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis. Read more: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?

recent_candidates.title: Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
recent_candidates.author: Mera Aladam
recent_candidates.excerpt: Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank have described how Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and sprayed racist graffiti on homes during overnight attacks on several villages. Footage from Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik on Sunday shows burnt-out cars and graffiti reading "Death to Arabs" and "Revenge" painted on walls. Residents said settlers attacked their villages while families were asleep, leaving multiple vehicles destroyed. "We were sleeping and not expecting that herds of settlers will attack our homes while people are sleeping, we never expected this," said Muneer Alkhatib, a resident of Deir Abu Mashal. Another resident, Montaser Almalki, said the attackers came from a nearby settler outpost and warned that his family could have been caught in a fire had they not woken up. The attacks took place across several locations in the occupied West Bank. They were condemned by Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who described them as "Jewish terrorism" and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for encouraging the violence. Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank have described how Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and sprayed racist graffiti on homes during overnight attacks on several villages. — Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) November 22, 2026

recent_candidates.title: Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
recent_candidates.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
recent_candidates.excerpt: Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon Israeli forces detonated explosives to destroy structures on the outskirts of Qantara in southern Lebanon , Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. Earlier on Sunday, Israeli forces set off a massive explosion in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, followed by another in Kfar Tibnit, according to NNA. The blasts could be heard across much of southern Lebanon. Residents of Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Zawtar held two separate protests against the Lebanese government's "silence" over Israel's occupation of areas up to the Litani River, which began in March, according to NNA. Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said he would not accept congratulations on Lebanon's Independence Day, which falls on 22 November, in solidarity with residents of the occupied southern border villages. In a statement, Berri described this year's independence as "incomplete and unfulfilled". He said it would be complete only once Lebanese territory was liberated and official and popular positions were united again.

Near Hizma, north-east of Jerusalem, Israeli forces fired live ammunition at Palestinian workers trying to cross the separation wall into the city, wounding several of them, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. Around 18 workers were detained, and video footage showed one of them being severely beaten. The Palestine Red Crescent said it treated two people who were injured after being beaten by Israeli forces and falling from the wall. Israeli forces later closed the entrances to Hizma and forced shops to shut. In al-Mughayyir, north-east of Ramallah, several Palestinians were injured by flying glass when settlers attacked vehicles on Sunday evening, the head of the village council, Amin Abu Alia, told Wafa. recent_candidates.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government
recent_candidates.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
recent_candidates.excerpt: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides. Delegations from Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday. “The latest round of coalition talks… has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,” the two parties said in a joint statement. “A follow-up meeting will be held,” they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details. A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government, with the possibility of a 14‑day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra‑Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men. Pedestrians walk past an advertisement featuring Benjamin Netanyahu (R) of the Likud party and leader of the Yashar party Gadi Eisenkot

recent_candidates.title: Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in northern and central Gaza
recent_candidates.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
recent_candidates.excerpt: Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in northern and central Gaza Israeli forces killed two Palestinians in separate attacks in the Gaza Strip on Sunday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. One was shot dead by Israeli gunfire in Jabalia, north of Gaza, on Sunday evening. Earlier in the evening, an Israeli quadcopter drone struck and killed another Palestinian in eastern Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza. recent_candidates.title: Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
recent_candidates.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
recent_candidates.excerpt: Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher, as senior military commanders touted the Islamic Republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States. "A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday. State television broadcast footage of Ahmad Vahidi, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC's Aerospace Force, touring an underground missile base. The two commanders were shown riding on top of a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment. "The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation," Vahidi said. "Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy," said Mousavi. During the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes targeted the country's missile capabilities and hit its nuclear sites for a second time, though the extent of the damage remains unclear. Earlier this month, the IRGC unveiled what it described as new underground "missile cities" housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers. recent_candidates.title: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
recent_candidates.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
recent_candidates.excerpt: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says Iran's navy said on Sunday that two supertankers hit naval mines and caught fire after entering a "restricted area" east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported. According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island. Both vessels reportedly stopped moving. Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker. The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses". UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman. It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described. recent_candidates.title: Recalibrating Counter-Transnational Criminal Organization Strategy in Belize
recent_candidates.author: Rogelio Ramirez
recent_candidates.excerpt: The Latin American (LATAM) and Caribbean Basin have been significantly stigmatized as a drug-trafficking region that harbors Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs). Nations in this region, including Belize, have been combating TCOs with varying degrees of success. These successes are measured by seizure statisticsand by the street value of confiscated drugs. Each year, various US-based publications provide a statistical x-ray (cross-section) of what each of these nations is doing to prevent primarily cocaine from entering the US. Based on these metrics, the country may be blacklisted and, to a degree, reprimanded for not doing enough tocontribute to the unified action of stopping the flow of drugs. The focus should not be primarily on supply-side interdiction and tactical enforcement, but on a more balanced approach that targets the state’s core vulnerabilities: corruption, systemic judicial impunity, and the socio-economic drivers of criminal recruitment. The current strategy used by countries and partners in the region to combat TCOs is ineffective, as a focus on supply-side interdiction and tactical enforcement has historically failed. Hence, a more balanced approach isneeded. The strategy being implemented has not worked and will not, but the “Balloon Effect” remains relevant at its core. recent_candidates.title: Andy Burnham’s EU delusion
recent_candidates.author: Wolfgang Munchau
recent_candidates.excerpt: Last Friday, Donald Trump was returning home from a summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. That same day, Russia launched a barrage of strikes on Ukraine, with two missiles and a jet-powered drone landing in Poland. And in the evening, the AI company Anthropic published a proof of the most intractable mathematical problem of all time — the Riemann hypothesis. Those three events encapsulate Europe’s three big strategic challenges: regaining geopolitical influence; bringing peace back to the continent; and catching up with the US and China on AI. Yet as all that unfolded, Andy Burnham was meeting EU leaders to negotiate a Brexit reset and their agenda focused on three quite different subjects: cheese, pet passports and youth mobility . When nations decline, this is exactly what happens. You won’t see tumbleweed rolling through ghost towns just yet — but you’ll hear people quarreling about cheese. Both sides are back in their pettiest of Brexit modes. Each new British prime minister thinks they can get a better deal, when in fact the EU will only ever offer a limited menu to external countries — the same one we all discussed endlessly during the Brexit wars. The Brussels officials doing the negotiating care mostly about stuff that no one else in Europe is bothered by, like expensive British schools or universities to which they can no longer afford to send their children. recent_candidates.title: Why Europe is bunkering down
recent_candidates.author: Juliette Bretan
recent_candidates.excerpt: There’s a secret beneath Helsinki. Dig 25 meters down beneath its granite crust, and you’ll find vast hockey pitches, brightly colored swimming pools, adventure playgrounds and the city’s first-ever axe-throwing venue. It’s called HELAXE, and notes on its website that “bowling is for pussies!”. Yet in a matter of hours, these spaces, one the size of a seven-story building, can be utterly transformed: the pitches removed and the pool water drained to be replaced with decontamination showers and enough bunk beds for 6,000 people. With the Russian frontier just 100 miles away, and Putin’s gray-zone operations ramping up, these are bunkers fit for an age of uncertainty. Helsinki has offered inspiration to a vast array of European leaders and delegations, each seeking to fashion their own approaches to shelters and civil defense. Across Europe, nations, cities, and even private citizens are reimagining subterranean space as we are told to prepare for a “Black Sky” event . It all reflects a distinct shift in the conception of conflict among its citizens. Where, in the past, wars might have seemed like something that happened in far-off fields, the rise in these dual-use bunkers, blending the mundane with the martial, suggests preparedness is increasingly becoming just another part of life. recent_candidates.title: En España, Vox está a las puertas del poder
recent_candidates.author: Ramona Bloj
recent_candidates.excerpt: Según una encuesta exclusiva de Cluster 17 realizada antes de las elecciones generales españolas del 29 de noviembre de 2026, el Partido Popular (PP), liderado por Alberto Núñez Feijóo (30,4%), está prácticamente empatado con el Partido Socialista Obrero Español (PSOE) de Pedro Sánchez (29,9%). Le siguen Vox (extrema derecha), liderado por Santiago Abascal, con un 18,4% de intención de voto, y Frente Amplio (5,8%). Se trata de un avance extraordinario para Vox, que había obtenido el 12,38% de los votos en las elecciones de 2023 y que parece haber logrado captar a una parte del electorado del PP. La izquierda también retrocede: Sumar, el partido de Yolanda Díaz, ahora integrado en el Frente Amplio, obtiene menos votos que en las anteriores elecciones (12,33%). La participación se estima en un 69%. Si estas intenciones de voto se confirmaran el día de las elecciones, el PP obtendría 125 escaños, el PSOE 120 y Vox 65. Con 190 diputados, el PP y Vox alcanzan la mayoría absoluta, mientras que el PSOE y sus aliados de izquierda se quedan en 150. Sin embargo, en una encuesta de Cluster-17 realizada a finales de octubre, el 54% de los encuestados consideraba inaceptable una coalición entre el PP y Vox. recent_candidates.title: Los autónomos reclaman «medidas eficaces» y «menos burocracia» en una manifestación
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: Unos 600 autónomos, según las cifras de Delegación de Gobierno, se han manifestado este domingo en Madrid para reclamar «medidas concretas, verificables y eficaces» que mejoren las condiciones de los trabajadores por cuenta propia y «menos burocracia», como ha expresado la organización de la protesta. «Este sistema de burocracia se tiene que terminar», ha afirmado uno de los portavoces. La marcha, convocada por la Plataforma por la Dignidad de los Autónomos y secundada por organizaciones como CEPA, FAENA, AUPA (Autónomos Unidos para Actuar), ANAM (Asociación Nacional de Arrastre del Mediterráneo), la Plataforma de Feriantes de Madrid, UNASPI, UNAMUR y la Plataforma de Imagen Personal Creer en nosotros, ha arrancado alrededor de las 12:00 horas en la plaza de España y ha recorrido parte de la Gran Vía y Callao hasta llegar a la plaza Cánovas del Castillo, donde ha concluido pasadas las 14:00 horas. El presidente de la Coordinadora Española de Profesionales Autónomos (CEPA), Daniel Bosseller, ha explicado este domingo que a la manifestación han acudido personas de toda España para reivindicar una legislación propia y «voz propia» en las mesas de negociación y en el Consejo de Autónomos y ha asegurado que «no ha cambiado absolutamente nada» en el último año al tiempo que ha pedido «un cambio radical de las reglas del juego, donde primero se trabaja, se gana dinero y luego se paga». recent_candidates.title: Bulgari, adiós a la ‘dolce vita’
recent_candidates.author: Javier Rioyo
recent_candidates.excerpt: Nunca vi sudar a Paolo Bulgari . Ya estuviéramos cerca del desierto, navegando por el Mediterráneo, en su riad palaciego de Marrakech, en una terraza romana, en Nápoles en ferragosto, en los veranos de Madrid o en una cala de Ibiza. Lo conocí una noche romana de mediados de los años noventa. Ya era la pareja —todavía sin «oficializar» la relación— de una de mis más queridas amigas, una joven compañera de los tiempos de Cueto, del nacimiento del Canal+ , que se iniciaba en el oficio entre la radio —la SER—, el periodismo escrito — El País — y los nuevos lenguajes de una televisión de modelo francés y experimento español. Ni la nostalgia ni la melancolía sirven de nada y no lloraremos sobre la leche derramada; tuvimos y seguimos contando con la amistad de Maite Carpio , así que pase la vida. Maite, la mujer de Paolo, nuestra amiga, es y siempre será el amor de sus últimos, felices, treinta años y la madre de dos adoradas hijas. Maite y Paolo tuvieron un flechazo, uno de esos encuentros capaces de unir pasión, amor, cercanía, convivencia y complicidad, sin que eso quiera decir que vivieran en una balsa de aceite. Su viaje tuvo mareas, peligros y cantos de sirena, sin dejar de compartir rumbo, cariño y una admiración en dos sentidos. Dos que supieron navegar juntos hasta el final. El sábado 21 de noviembre murió en su eterna Roma el más refinado de los joyeros, el condottiere de Via Condotti. El lunes 23, en la Basílica di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme , se habrá celebrado su funera

recent_candidates.title: El temporal de viento deja 12 heridos en Cataluña, dos de ellos graves
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: A diferencia de ayer, la jornada del domingo está marcada por cielos despejados y temperaturas más frías, pero sobre todo por el fuerte viento que ha provocado en Cataluña heridas a 12 personas, dos de ellas graves por la caída de árboles, informa Europa Press. Protección Civil mantiene activo su plan de prevención VENCAT por este temporal de viento, que puede dejar rachas máximas de entre los 70 y 80 kilómetros por hora en buena parte del territorio, incluida Barcelona, cuyo ayuntamiento activó también anoche su plan de emergencias. En esta ciudad una persona ha quedado herida grave al caerle encima un árbol en el cruce de la calle Marina con la avenida Icària, en el barrio de la Vila Olímpica. La otra persona que se encuentra grave estaba en Matadepera (Barcelona), cuando un árbol ha caído sobre un vehículo en la carretera BV-1221. Ambas fueron trasladadas al hospital. Galicia, en alerta por lluvias persistentes y fuertes vientos de hasta 80 kilómetros por hora THE OBJECTIVE La mayor parte de las personas afectadas por el viento participaban en una carrera popular. recent_candidates.title: Tropas rusas toman el control de otra localidad en el noreste de Ucrania
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: El Ministerio de Defensa de Rusia ha anunciado este domingo que sus tropas han asumido el control de Sosnovi Bor, una localidad situada en la región de Járkov, en el noreste de Ucrania , tras una operación del grupo de fuerzas Norte. «Como resultado de operaciones enérgicas, se ha establecido el control sobre la localidad de Sosnovi Bor», ha señalado el departamento militar ruso en un comunicado difundido a través de Telegram. Asimismo, Moscú ha informado de que sus Fuerzas Armadas han llevado a cabo durante esta pasada noche ataques con drones contra instalaciones energéticas, infraestructuras portuarias y embarcaciones que, según sostiene, prestaban apoyo al Ejército ucraniano . Entre los objetivos alcanzados figuran la central eléctrica Pravoberezhnaya, de 330 kilovoltios, en Zaporiyia, instalaciones del puerto de Kiliya, en la región de Odesa, y un buque de carga seca que transportaba mercancías de doble uso para las fuerzas ucranianas mientras navegaba al noreste de Odesa. Rusia asegura haber derribado 170 drones ucranianos durante la noche en siete regiones THE OBJECTIVE Por otra parte, el Ministerio de Defensa ruso ha asegurado que sus sistemas de defensa antiaérea han «interceptado y destruido» durante la noche hasta 170 vehículos aéreos no tripulados ucranianos en distintas regiones del país, así como en la península de Crimea y en aguas de los mares de Azov y Negro.

recent_candidates.excerpt: Las autoridades militares mexicanas han confirmado este sábado la muerte de once personas en enfrentamientos durante la operación llevada a cabo para la detención de Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, alias El Chapo Isidro , líder del Cártel de Guasave o Los Mazatlecos y uno de los diez criminales más buscados por el FBI , en la localidad de Guasave, en el estado mexicano de Sinaloa. Durante esta operación han fallecido siete miembros del Cártel y cuatro soldados del Ejército mexicano que se dirigían a reforzar la seguridad en el municipio de Guasave ante una fuerte resistencia de los integrantes del grupo criminal, según ha informado el Ministerio de Defensa mexicano en sus redes sociales. recent_candidates.title: Democracia 21 rechaza la idea del «voto útil que reivindican» PP y PSOE
recent_candidates.author: Manu Torralba
recent_candidates.excerpt: La candidata del partido Democracia 21 para las elecciones generales del 29-N, Miriam González , ha cuestionado que haya un «voto útil», como reivindican los grandes partidos, Partido Popular y PSOE y ha reprochado que no hayan llegado a acuerdos en cuestiones como el acceso a la vivienda, la reforma educativa o el mantenimiento de las infraestructuras. «La gente primero. El partido después» , ha señalado. Además, en el acto central de la campaña que ha celebrado esta semana el partido en Madrid, González se ha comprometido a recortar «radicalmente» las subvenciones a los partidos políticos, acabar con las presiones que hacen a los periodistas y apartar a los partidos de los medios públicos. «Prioridad nacional por los jóvenes» Para Democracia 21, la «prioridad nacional» son los jóvenes. Por ello, entre las medidas defendidas por su líder, figuran un Plan de Barrios para ampliar la oferta de vivienda asequible, la eliminación de impuestos sobre la vivienda para jóvenes y una educación con más formación práctica, tecnológica y económica.
